scope: Q5 collector and verifier with actual Electron, Pi, visible UI controls, original SQLite/Pi readback and the fixed public source. Model POSTs are served only by a TEMP loopback fixture. This is not the 32-row paid ABBA.

negativeControls: An actual loopback POST reserved and prebound to the wrong Run stops the collector. The original reservation and used count remain after reopen.
A fixed website HTTP 200 without the original native receipt cannot be reported as a read.
Late or unknown Run IDs cannot dispatch across a newly activated segment.
An acknowledged terminal failure without a POST keeps the first Run's charged attempt attached. A zero-request segment cannot pass collection.
The schedule remains 32 task rows even when a Q5 row has two Run segments.

electronPair.fixtureAdapter: A TEMP copy replaces both fixed live upstream endpoints with 127.0.0.1, supplies a fake model key, blocks direct model requests, and points the B launcher at the tested production compile. The app code, counting proxy, ledger implementation and real public website path are unchanged.

attempts.finding: Continuation ended before model dispatch with event_persistence. The first two fixture requests remained spent.
Continuation received HTTP 200, then event_persistence. The native tool recorded cancelled, no success receipt was committed, and approval was uncertain. The collector reports no source read.

The same application build passed in a fresh profile. A stderr listener added to the diagnostic driver did not alter application behavior. Approval was consumed once, and the fixed source receipt matched after close.
Final collector including failure preservation passed on the same app build. Same-task continuation received HTTP 200, with identical hot and cold native receipt hashes.

priorFailures.finding: B was launched while its renderer build was still in progress; the first B attempt never reached model dispatch. A passed.

Electron's evaluation callback received the Electron module as its first argument. The initial per-Run diagnostic therefore lost the segment timestamp and did not recognize a real HTTP 200. Forward the explicit segment ID as the second argument; same fixture then passed.
